images.title: Before one or past one
images.purpose: Show that some fraction lengths end before the mark 1 and some end after it, so a fraction can be more than one unit.
images.composition: One long number line across the frame, the stretch before 1 lightly shaded on one side, with one point on each side of 1 and well spaced labels.
images.exact_structure: A grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 2 with exactly 3 ticks, at 0, 1 and 2, evenly spaced. The tick at 1 is bold reddish purple #CC79A7. The stretch from 0 to 1 is very lightly shaded teal; the stretch from 1 to 2 is plain. A teal #0072B2 point sits two thirds of the way from 0 to 1. An amber #E69F00 point sits exactly halfway between 1 and 2. Exactly 1 number line, 2 points.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
the 3/2 point placed before 1, or the 2/3 point placed after 1
images.takeaway: A fraction that ends after 1 is more than one unit.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 2 with the mark 1 in bold; a teal point at 2/3 sits before 1 and an amber point at 3/2 sits halfway between 1 and 2.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the bold mark 1 and say which side each point is on.

image_decisions.why: Ending before or after the mark 1 is a position idea that one number line shows directly.
